audit.whatIsWrong: Lane-difficulty text leaned on a nonexistent Aatrox revive to explain the level 6 swing.
audit.why: Riot's current World Ender text grants AD, increased healing and Move Speed and fears nearby minions, extended on a takedown. No revive. The aatrox-side mirror audit already corrected this.
audit.corrected: Difficulty framing kept EVEN 5.5/10; the level 6 edge is restated as the execute floor beating his healing amp, not a revive.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes and late-game text gave no real cooldown figures and whys[5] described level 6 while sitting in the First item row.
audit.why: World Ender is 120/100/80s and Aatrox Q is 14s at rank 1; those numbers make the commit windows concrete. whys[5] is the First-item row, so it must describe the Lich Bane spike.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] now names the 120s cooldown, late names the 80s late-rank figure, early names the 14s Q, whys[5] now describes the first-item Lich Bane spike.

audit.whatIsWrong: Locke's Q was called "Ritual Nails" and the passive "Silver Stake"; Aatrox's R was credited with a revive.
audit.why: Locke's Q text in the kit reads Soul Nails. The passive has no name in the kit text, so no name is asserted. Aatrox R has no revive.
audit.corrected: Q referred to as Soul Nails; passive referred to generically; World Ender described as a healing/AD amp with the E dash (Umbral Dash, 9/8/7/6/5s) as his gap-closer.

audit.why: Aatrox W (Infernal Chains) carries a derived grounding flag that Riot's description does not support — it drags and slows only. The page never claimed grounding, so nothing to fix.

edits.before: Locke favoured at 6 — R Purgatory executes through his revive window.
edits.after: Locke favoured on first item — Lich Bane makes the blink-consume bite lethal.

edits.before: Your R Purgatory totem drops him into execute range before his World Ender revive can bail him out, so an all-in here is your cleanest kill window of the lane.
edits.after: Your R Purgatory totem drops him under the execute floor, and World Ender only amps his healing — there is no revive — so commit while its 120s cooldown is still burning.

edits.before: Grouped, his revive plus healing sustains through fights while your burst gets kited; you need to isolate a target and blow R before he engages.
edits.after: Grouped, his World Ender healing amp grinds through your burst while you get kited; isolate a target and blow R before Umbral Dash closes the gap.

edits.before: After items his revive and healing let him grind through your burst unless you time R Purgatory on his World Ender, which is exactly your Level 6 edge before the game evens back out.
edits.after: After items his healing amp lets him grind through your burst unless you save R Purgatory for after World Ender ends — its 80s late cooldown is your window before the game evens back out.

edits.before: Force extended trades where his passive and revive win
edits.after: Force extended trades where his passive healing wins

edits.before: Levels 1-2 are a pure skill lane: Aatrox out-ranges you with Q but his early cooldowns are long, so trade with Ritual Nails autos when his Q is down and respect the sweet-spot heals.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 are a pure skill lane: Aatrox out-ranges you with Q but it is down 14s at rank 1, so trade with Soul Nails marks in that gap and respect the sweet-spot heals.

edits.before: Aatrox wants to hit all three Q edges and heal off you; sidestep the sweet spots and punish the long recovery with Q Ritual Nails autos so his sustain never gets going.
edits.after: Aatrox wants to hit all three Q edges and heal off you; sidestep the sweet spots and punish the long recovery with Soul Nails marks so his sustain never gets going.

edits.before: Through 3-6 it stays even because he wants to land layered Q sweet spots while you weave in P Silver Stake on-hits and use E Ashen Pursuit to dodge them; whoever executes cleaner wins the exchange.
edits.after: Through 3-6 it stays even because he wants layered Q sweet spots while you weave in passive on-hits and use E Ashen Pursuit, up every 10s, to dodge them; whoever executes cleaner wins.

notes: "Silver Stake" as Locke's passive name is not in the kit file (passive has no name field), so it was removed rather than reused; if it is the real name, restore it.
